title: Restaurant host
does: Greets guests, manages a wait list, answers basic questions, and helps keep the entrance organized.
suits: A calm, friendly teen who likes people and can stay organized during busy periods.
find: Restaurants, diners, hotel restaurants, and local cafés; ask for the manager during a quiet period.
start: Prepare a short introduction, list your school-safe availability, and ask whether host training is provided.
skills: Clear communication, patience, basic counting, and learning the restaurant’s seating system.
schedule: Usually after school, evenings, weekends, and holiday rushes; late shifts may have age limits.
safety: Ask who supervises the front of house, how late shifts end, and which local youth-work rules apply.

title: Server assistant
does: Refills water, clears used dishes, resets tables, and helps servers keep service moving.
suits: Someone energetic who notices details and is comfortable moving through a crowded room.
find: Family restaurants, cafés, banquet rooms, and busy seasonal restaurants.
start: Ask for a support role and be ready to explain that you can follow instructions and keep a steady pace.
skills: Teamwork, safe carrying, listening, cleanliness, and remembering several small tasks.
schedule: Commonly weekend and dinner shifts; hours can change with reservations and events.
safety: Learn safe lifting and hot-surface rules; never carry more than you can control.

title: Dishwasher
does: Sorts dishes, loads washing equipment, keeps the dish area clean, and supports kitchen flow.
suits: A dependable teen who prefers clear physical tasks and can work carefully when it is loud.
find: Restaurants, cafeterias, retirement communities, camps, and event kitchens.
start: Ask about training, equipment, footwear, and whether the schedule can fit school.
skills: Consistency, sanitation habits, safe chemical handling, and stamina.
schedule: Often evenings, weekends, and summer shifts; closing work can run late.
safety: Use required gloves and footwear, learn chemical labels, and report broken glass or unsafe floors.

title: Prep cook assistant
does: Washes produce, measures ingredients, labels containers, and completes simple prep under supervision.
suits: A focused teen who enjoys food and can follow a recipe or checklist exactly.
find: Restaurants, bakeries, cafés, catering kitchens, and school food programs.
start: Mention safe kitchen habits, ask what tasks are allowed for your age, and learn the kitchen’s food-safety process.
skills: Measuring, knife-safety basics, cleanliness, timing, and following written directions.
schedule: May include mornings, weekends, or after-school prep depending on the kitchen.
safety: Do not use restricted equipment without training and supervision; ask about burns, cuts, and allergy procedures.

title: Bakery assistant
does: Packages baked goods, labels orders, cleans work areas, and helps with simple decorating or prep.
suits: A careful teen who likes routines, presentation, and working with food.
find: Independent bakeries, grocery bakeries, cafés, and farmers-market vendors.
start: Bring photos of a permitted home baking project only if requested, and ask what training is needed.
skills: Attention to detail, measuring, packaging, customer service, and basic food hygiene.
schedule: Early mornings and weekends are common; holiday seasons may be especially busy.
safety: Ask about ovens, mixers, allergens, and lifting; follow local rules for food handling.

title: Café counter worker
does: Takes orders, prepares simple drinks or food, handles payments, and keeps the counter stocked.
suits: A social teen who can switch between conversation, accuracy, and cleanup.
find: Coffee shops, campus cafés, bookstores with cafés, and neighborhood breakfast spots.
start: Ask whether the employer hires trainees and practice repeating orders clearly before applying.
skills: Customer service, basic arithmetic, food hygiene, memory, and multitasking.
schedule: Morning, weekend, and after-school shifts vary by location; opening shifts may start early.
safety: Learn hot-drink and equipment procedures; confirm who handles cash and customer complaints.

title: Ice-cream shop attendant
does: Serves customers, prepares cones or cups, operates a register, and cleans the shop.
suits: An upbeat teen who enjoys short customer interactions and can keep a cheerful pace.
find: Ice-cream shops, dessert counters, amusement areas, and seasonal boardwalk businesses.
start: Visit during a quiet time, ask about seasonal hiring, and bring a simple availability list.
skills: Portioning, cleanliness, counting change, friendly service, and teamwork.
schedule: Often afternoons, evenings, weekends, and summer; seasonal hours can change quickly.
safety: Ask about freezer exposure, wet floors, closing transport, and food-allergy procedures.

title: Grocery deli assistant
does: Packages prepared foods, labels containers, restocks displays, and helps customers find items.
suits: A tidy, helpful teen who can follow sanitation and labeling rules.
find: Supermarkets, specialty grocers, food halls, and neighborhood markets.
start: Ask what deli tasks are permitted for your age and whether the store provides food-safety training.
skills: Organization, customer service, hygiene, labeling, and careful product handling.
schedule: After-school and weekend shifts are common; holidays can bring extra hours.
safety: Ask before using slicers, hot equipment, or cleaning chemicals; report allergens and spills.

title: Catering assistant
does: Packs supplies, sets tables, carries light items, serves guests, and helps clean up events.
suits: A flexible team player who likes variety and can follow a lead person’s instructions.
find: Catering companies, banquet halls, community centers, and event venues.
start: Ask about event dates, transportation, uniform requirements, and the exact lifting expectations.
skills: Punctuality, presentation, teamwork, safe carrying, and polite guest service.
schedule: Mostly weekends, evenings, and one-time events; shifts may be irregular.
safety: Confirm how you get home after events and do not lift hot, heavy, or unstable items alone.

title: Food-truck helper
does: Takes orders, restocks supplies, cleans surfaces, and helps a small crew serve customers.
suits: An adaptable teen who can work in tight spaces and communicate clearly in a rush.
find: Food trucks, farmers markets, festivals, and mobile catering businesses.
start: Ask about the truck’s route, shift length, weather plan, and food-safety training.
skills: Customer service, organization, cash or tablet accuracy, and working as a small team.
schedule: Events and lunch periods create varied shifts; outdoor work depends on weather.
safety: Ask about generator, propane, hot-surface, traffic, and hand-washing procedures.

title: Concession stand attendant
does: Sells snacks and drinks, handles payments, restocks supplies, and cleans a public food area.
suits: A quick, friendly teen who can stay accurate while lines are moving.
find: Movie theaters, sports venues, pools, fairs, and school event concessions.
start: Ask about event schedules, cash handling, and whether the role includes late-night closing.
skills: Counting, speed, customer service, stocking, and basic food hygiene.
schedule: Part-time event shifts, evenings, weekends, and school holidays.
safety: Know where the supervisor is, keep walkways clear, and use equipment only after training.

title: Juice or smoothie counter worker
does: Takes orders, prepares simple drinks, cleans blenders and counters, and manages ingredients.
suits: An energetic teen who likes routines, food, and short customer conversations.
find: Juice bars, gyms, cafés, markets, and health-food shops.
start: Ask about recipes, equipment training, allergy procedures, and school-year scheduling.
skills: Following recipes, cleanliness, measuring, customer service, and safe equipment use.
schedule: Often after school, mornings, weekends, and summer.
safety: Learn blender and electrical safety, disclose allergies, and follow sanitation instructions.

title: Hotel front-desk assistant
does: Welcomes guests, answers basic questions, organizes supplies, and supports the front desk team.
suits: A polished, patient teen who communicates well and can protect guest privacy.
find: Hotels, hostels, resorts, and conference centers; ask about trainee or lobby-support roles.
start: Prepare examples of reliability and ask whether the role includes guest check-in or only supervised support.
skills: Professional communication, basic computer use, organization, and confidentiality.
schedule: Day, evening, weekend, and holiday shifts; overnight work may be restricted.
safety: Know the supervisor, avoid sharing guest information, and confirm safe transport after closing.

title: Housekeeping assistant
does: Helps prepare rooms or shared spaces, replaces supplies, and reports maintenance issues.
suits: A dependable teen who likes visible results and can work carefully without constant reminders.
find: Hotels, vacation rentals with a formal company, camps, and conference centers.
start: Ask about room assignments, cleaning products, lifting, and who checks your work.
skills: Thoroughness, time management, respectful privacy, and safe cleaning habits.
schedule: Often daytime, weekends, and peak travel seasons.
safety: Never enter a room without the required process; learn chemical labels and report hazards.

title: Hotel laundry attendant
does: Sorts linens, loads approved machines, folds supplies, and keeps the laundry area organized.
suits: A methodical teen who prefers behind-the-scenes work and repeated processes.
find: Hotels, resorts, hospitals, camps, and commercial laundry departments.
start: Ask about machine training, heat exposure, lifting, and the exact age requirements.
skills: Sorting, stamina, organization, label reading, and consistency.
schedule: Daytime and weekend shifts are common; travel seasons may increase demand.
safety: Use required protective equipment, avoid overloaded carts, and never mix chemicals without instruction.

title: Event setup assistant
does: Places chairs, signs, linens, light decorations, and supplies before a meeting or event.
suits: A practical teen who enjoys changing projects and can follow a floor plan.
find: Hotels, event venues, community centers, theaters, and conference companies.
start: Ask what equipment you may use, how long events run, and whether a supervisor stays on site.
skills: Teamwork, spatial awareness, punctuality, and careful carrying.
schedule: Mostly one-time events, weekends, and evenings.
safety: Use two-person lifts, keep exits clear, and do not climb ladders or move heavy equipment without training.

title: Camp counselor
does: Leads approved activities, supervises campers, models routines, and reports concerns to senior staff.
suits: A responsible teen who likes working with younger children and can stay alert.
find: Day camps, recreation departments, community centers, and nonprofit summer programs.
start: Ask about minimum age, background-check rules, first aid, training, and the counselor-to-camper plan.
skills: Patience, activity planning, communication, conflict de-escalation, and reliability.
schedule: Usually daytime summer work, sometimes with pre-season training.
safety: Follow child-protection, water, pickup, emergency, and one-on-one contact rules exactly.

title: Recreation aide
does: Sets up activities, checks equipment, welcomes participants, and helps staff run a safe program.
suits: An active teen who enjoys sports, games, or community programming.
find: Parks departments, gyms, community centers, pools, and youth clubs.

skills: Organization, encouragement, basic equipment checks, and clear boundaries.
schedule: After school, weekends, summers, and program-specific blocks.
safety: Follow participant check-in rules, report injuries, and do not supervise outside your assigned role.

title: Lifeguard
does: Monitors swimmers, enforces pool rules, and responds to emergencies within trained procedures.
suits: A focused teen who is a strong swimmer and willing to complete required certification.
find: Public pools, private clubs, water parks, camps, and recreation centers.
start: Find an approved lifeguard course, pass the prerequisites, and ask about minimum age and renewal dates.
skills: Swimming, scanning, emergency response, communication, and sustained attention.
schedule: Seasonal summer, weekends, and scheduled pool blocks.
safety: Certification and supervision are essential; never accept the role without the required training.

title: Ticketing attendant
does: Scans tickets, answers directions questions, manages a queue, and helps guests reach the right area.
suits: A composed teen who likes short interactions and can follow event procedures.

start: Ask about event dates, dress code, ticket scanners, and the supervisor’s location.
skills: Attention to detail, polite communication, technology comfort, and crowd awareness.
schedule: Mostly evenings, weekends, and event dates.
safety: Know emergency exits and crowd procedures; never leave a post without coverage.

title: Guest-services assistant
does: Provides directions, prepares information materials, answers routine questions, and escalates problems.

skills: Listening, local knowledge, organization, and knowing when to ask for help.
schedule: Daytime, weekends, holidays, and tourist seasons.
safety: Protect visitor information and follow lost-child, emergency, and incident-reporting procedures.

title: Museum visitor assistant

safety: Follow exhibit, emergency, and visitor-boundary rules; do not touch restricted objects.

title: Tour support assistant

find: Walking-tour companies, historic homes, visitor centers, and attractions.

skills: Public communication, timekeeping, local research, and group awareness.
schedule: Weekends, holidays, and tourist seasons; weather can change plans.

title: Wedding venue assistant

suits: An organized teen who can stay calm around time-sensitive details.
find: Event venues, hotels, banquet spaces, and wedding coordination companies.
start: Ask about event hours, transportation home, dress expectations, and which tasks are supervised.
skills: Checklist use, communication, presentation, and careful movement around guests.
schedule: Mostly weekend events and occasional evenings.
safety: Keep exits clear, do not lift unstable décor, and know who handles emergencies or guest conflict.

safety: Ask about ventilation, solvents, lead or mold hazards, and ladder rules before accepting work.

title: Construction site cleanup assistant

title: Fence installation helper

skills: Measuring, teamwork, stamina, and following a layout.

safety: Check for underground utilities and tool restrictions; only trained adults should handle hazardous equipment.

title: Pressure-washing helper

title: Moving crew helper

skills: Packing, communication, spatial judgment, stamina, and care with property.

title: Flooring helper
category: Jobs in Construction and Skilled Trades
does: Prepares supplies, measures rooms, cleans surfaces, and assists with supervised installation work.
suits: A precise teen who likes patterns, measuring, and hands-on projects.
find: Flooring retailers, installers, remodeling contractors, and trade-school programs.

skills: Curiosity, punctuality, measurement, safety habits, and willingness to practice.

safety: Read the training agreement and confirm which tools, heights, chemicals, or machines are off-limits.

skills: Tool care, diagnosis, patience, organization, and customer explanation.

safety: Use eye protection and correct tools; do not test a repair until a qualified adult checks it.

safety: Pool chemicals can be hazardous; minors should not mix or handle restricted chemicals without approved supervision.
